title: US blockade and Hormuz shipping standoff continue
summary: The US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and Iran still restricts the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran says it will use all available means against the blockade, which it calls military aggression.
Iran's navy said on 23 November that three tankers hit mines in Hormuz. UKMTO had not confirmed mines earlier.
why_it_matters: About one fifth of world oil normally passed the strait, so the standoff affects energy prices and shipping worldwide.
verify_note: Iran's mine claims, including three tankers on 23 November reported by CBS, were not confirmed by UKMTO. Latest weekly transit count was not found.

title: How the US-Iran war reached today's standoff
summary: The US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February 2026. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed.
A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire began in April. A June memorandum promised an end to fighting and talks toward a final deal.
Fighting resumed in July after ship attacks. Now there is neither full war nor peace.
why_it_matters: Every current question, from the blockade to the nuclear stock, comes from the war that began on 28 February and its failed deals.
verify_note: Sources differ by a day or so on some dates: ceasefire 7 or 8 April, memorandum announced 14 June and called the 17 June memorandum elsewhere. Signing was planned for 19 June, per France 24.

sources.title: US-Iran war, then and now: How the landscape has changed since February
sources.supports: Strikes began 28 February during nuclear talks. Khamenei was killed and his son Mojtaba succeeded him. Brent rose from $72 to a peak above $126.

sources.title: Pakistan army chief in Tehran: Can diplomacy prevent new US-Iran fighting?

The Guards say they hit US radars at two Bahrain bases on 21 November.
A US official says no US forces were damaged. Bahrain rejects the Guards' account; injury reports differ.

verify_note: Disputed: the Guards claim hits on US radars; a US official says there was no US damage. Bahrain's Interior Ministry reports no injuries; its Foreign Ministry reports two, per Iran International. CENTCOM denied a new Qeshm strike on 20 November.

title: Iran's uranium stock unchecked as IAEA is blocked
summary: At the IAEA board around 19 November, four Western powers urged Iran to let inspectors back in.
IAEA chief Grossi said only the undamaged Bushehr plant was inspected last quarter.
Iran has not said where its enriched uranium is. It asks whether the demand serves a new attack.
why_it_matters: Without inspections nobody can verify whether Iran is rebuilding a weapons-capable programme, which is the US core demand.
verify_note: The 19 November IAEA board pressure rests on one Reuters report, carried by Al-Monitor. The 440 kg figure is the IAEA's pre-June-2025 estimate. A second outlet on the board meeting was not found.

title: Iran's oil exports halted by blockade
summary: Kpler says Iran loaded no crude in September or October. Reuters carried the data.
Kpler counts about 20 loaded tankers idle near Kharg Island, holding 43 million barrels.
Iran's foreign ministry calls tanker loading reports speculation. Trump says blockade runners would be sunk.
why_it_matters: Iran lost about 200 to 250 million dollars a day in oil revenue, Kpler estimates. That pressure explains talk of testing the blockade.
verify_note: Trackers differ: Bloomberg dated the Kharg halt to late August; Kpler reports no loadings in September or October. Windward separately counts 31 laden sanctioned tankers near the blockade line in the Arabian Sea. A tanker run is unconfirmed: Tasnim says plans are being drawn up; officials say there is no concrete convoy plan.

title: Houthis launch near daily strikes on Saudi Arabia
summary: Since 7 November the Houthis say they attack Saudi Arabia almost daily, hitting oil sites, airports and bases.
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a Houthi missile and drone over the weekend of 21 to 22 November.
The Houthis say Saudi strikes on Hodeida killed 17 people by 23 November.

verify_note: The Hodeida toll rests on Houthi statements reported by CBS (23 November). Near daily Houthi attacks are reported by Al Jazeera and the Long War Journal, run by the FDD think tank. Saudi officials report shrapnel damage to an Aramco building and a pipeline fire.

Gaza's health ministry says 1,661 people were killed since the truce began, nine in two days of strikes.
The US-backed Board of Peace warned the truce could collapse and may hand reconstruction to the UN.
why_it_matters: If the truce collapses, displaced families in Gaza face renewed war while flooding already hits their tent shelters.
verify_note: Death tolls come from Gaza's health ministry and cannot be independently checked. Israel says its strikes target Hamas regrouping; Hamas calls the raid a violation. The Board of Peace adviser's remarks were made to Israeli outlet Ynet, read through The National.

The UN force's mandate ends on 31 December. Lebanon wants a replacement; Hezbollah rejects disarming.
why_it_matters: Without agreement on who verifies disarmament, a security gap could open in south Lebanon when UNIFIL leaves.
verify_note: A claim that the US and Israel favour private contractors comes only from Antiwar.com, an advocacy outlet, and is left out. Israeli think-tank reporting that Lebanon sees no point in another talks round before Israel's government forms was not opened directly.

sources.title: Ethiopia: Overnight Drone, Artillery Strikes Reported Around Badme Amid Ethiopian, Eritrean Military Buildup
sources.supports: Residents report drone and artillery fire near Badme; a diplomat says Eritrea reinforced positions. Eritrea accused Ethiopia's ruling party of expansionism on 18 November.

sources.title: Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of leading Tigray rebel offensive with Egyptian support
sources.supports: Ethiopia's army chief says Eritrea led a fourth rebel offensive with Egyptian supplies. Not independently verified; Eritrea and Egypt reject earlier similar claims.

sources.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea accuse one another of launching war
sources.supports: Ethiopia told the UN Eritrean troops advanced up to 60 km into Tigray. Eritrea calls itself the target.

sources.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea break ties: Does the conflict risk becoming regional war?
sources.supports: Eritrea cut ties on 1 October. Analysts fear spread to Sudan and Egypt.

title: Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen, truce deadline stays
summary: The US-China trade truce runs to 10 January. China extended its rare earth export pause on 9 November.
Trump and Xi met in Shenzhen on 19 November. The reports read name no change to the truce.
The US widened AI chip licence rules on 16 November. China warned of countermeasures, Fortune reported.
why_it_matters: The two largest economies control tariffs, chips and rare earths that affect factories and prices worldwide.
verify_note: Whether the truce terms changed at Shenzhen is not confirmed: CNBC and Fortune report the meeting but no truce outcome. The chip rule and China's warning rest on Fortune (18 November).

sources.title: Trump says he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged
sources.supports: Shenzhen meeting produced few concrete deliverables. Bessent says H200 chip policy is unchanged. Leaders agreed humans should stay in control of major military AI decisions.

sources.title: What's at stake for Trump and Xi in Shenzhen: A trade truce deadline, new export controls, and Iran
sources.supports: Truce ends 10 January. US widened AI chip licence rules on 16 November; Beijing warned of countermeasures. Analysts expected no final deal in Shenzhen.

sources.title: China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months
sources.supports: China extended the pause on some export controls to 10 January and suspended a 24% tariff. The US extended 178 exclusions.

sources.title: China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January
sources.supports: China's commerce ministry extended the suspension of some export controls to 10 January 2027.

title: Jihadists and rebels press Mali's military junta
summary: In April, al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and Tuareg separatists (FLA) attacked army sites across Mali. The defence minister was killed.
Mali's army says it retook Kidal on 6 October with Russian help. The rebels say they chose to leave.
JNIM took the Dioura army camp on 10 September. Death tolls range from 50 to 130 soldiers.
why_it_matters: ACLED counts about 3,400 deaths from militant attacks in Mali in early 2026. AP said JNIM had imposed a fuel blockade on Bamako.
verify_note: Disputed: the Dioura toll is at least 50 per AFP sources and 120 to 130 per Reuters sources; JNIM claims 150. Nothing credible newer than 6 October was found; a 2 November attack rests only on a JNIM claim.

sources.title: Al Qaeda-linked militants kill more than 100 Malian soldiers in attack this month, sources say
sources.supports: Security source says 130 soldiers died at Dioura on 10 September; a diplomat says about 120. JNIM claims 150. The army gave no figure.

sources.title: Mali's army says it has taken Kidal from Tuareg rebels, with Russia's help
sources.supports: Army says it retook Kidal with Russia's Africa Corps. The FLA calls it a controlled withdrawal.

sources.title: At least 50 soldiers killed in jihadist attack on Malian army base
sources.supports: JNIM claimed the Dioura camp; AFP sources said at least 50 soldiers died.

sources.title: What to know about the conflict in Mali and the world's most terrorized region
sources.supports: JNIM and FLA joined forces in April. Deaths up 35% in 2026. JNIM is expanding towards coastal states.

title: US pushes Venezuela court overhaul before elections
summary: US forces captured President Maduro on 3 January 2026, AP reported. Delcy Rodriguez is acting president.
On 9 November Rubio said new Supreme Court justices should sit by mid-December, then a new electoral council.
Rubio says Rodriguez should then declare the presidency vacant, starting a six-month window for elections.
why_it_matters: Washington shapes Venezuela's politics and oil, which affects the region and fuel prices.
verify_note: The mid-December timeline is Rubio's own statement, not an official Venezuelan announcement. Venezuela's assembly moved the justice application deadline to 18 November; whether it was met was not found. Machado returned 25 October and is excluded from the US-backed talks, per search summaries.

sources.title: Marco Rubio estima que el TSJ en Venezuela este constituido a mediados de diciembre
sources.supports: Rubio, at a G7 meeting in Paris, said the court should be seated by mid-December, then the electoral council, then a vacancy declaration and elections within six months.

sources.title: Venezuela Pushes Supreme Court Nomination Deadline to Nov. 18, And Rubio Is Counting Down to December
sources.supports: Venezuela's assembly moved the justice application deadline to 18 November. Final candidate list due 11 December; confirmation vote date not set.

sources.title: US urges Venezuela to follow phased plan for democratic transition
sources.supports: Rubio met Foreign Minister Blanco on 2 November. The US plan has three phases. Rodriguez gave no election date.

sources.title: Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart as US presses for progress on election preparations
sources.supports: Rubio urged release of remaining political prisoners; elections targeted for 2027.

title: Russian missiles and drone fall inside Poland
summary: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell in its southeast on 20 November. No injuries were reported.
Prime Minister Tusk called it an 'intentional provocation'. NATO chief Rutte called it a 'grave violation'.
Poland asked NATO for more support. Trump said the missiles landed 'by mistake'. No Russian response was reported.
why_it_matters: Russian weapons landing in a NATO state test the alliance's response, during a heavy Russian strike on Ukraine.
verify_note: Intent is disputed: Tusk calls it a provocation, Trump says a mistake. Later reports give three missiles; this card uses the first official count. Trump's remark rests on Al Jazeera.

sources.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
sources.supports: Polish defence minister says two missiles and a drone fell in the southeast; Tusk, Rutte and Burnham reactions; Trump says by mistake; Article 4 not invoked.

sources.title: Tusk denounces Russian 'provocation' after Warsaw says missiles crash in Poland
sources.supports: Two missiles and a jet drone crashed in eastern Poland; a Kh-101 landed near Nowy Lipowiec; no injuries reported; Tusk calls it a provocation.
